tmp:3218: yere Shabbat — one who fears Shabbat: fear of God attained in the Shabbat state, contrasted with weekday fear mixed with foolishness (LM on Shabbat-yirah with Da'at)
tmp:3219: ta'anug ve-simchah shel Shabbat — the delight and joy of Shabbat as a devotional state, source of complete fear-with-Da'at, opposed to weekday servitude
tmp:3221: yirah bi-shleimut im Da'at — fear of God in completeness, i.e. fear joined with mature awareness (Da'at), free of the foolishness of Job 4:6
tmp:3223: ha-pilosofim ve-ha-kofrim — the philosophers and heretics as a class of persons who allegorize the whole Torah and its practical mitzvot into mere 'form and intellect'
tmp:3224: even negef be-khol chokhmah — the 'stumbling stone' lurking within each of the seven secular wisdoms, identified as the aspect of Amalek that causes the inquirer to fall into heresy
tmp:3226: mitat ha-ishah ha-harah — the death of the struck pregnant woman (Ex 21:22 'ason'), symbolizing destruction of the hidden path/wisdom itself as punishment-scenario, not mere miscarriage
tmp:3227: ha-derekh chokhmah be-atzmo — the 'way of wisdom' itself (Prov 4:11), the new spiritual path in gestation, which strife may ruin along with its premature offspring
tmp:3228: ishah harah — the pregnant woman of Ex 21:22 as symbol of a spiritual path still in gestation/concealment before its revelation to the world
tmp:3229: ha-mefursamim she-na'asin kodem zemanam — leaders who become famous before their time, spiritual 'stillbirths' (nefalim) expelled prematurely by strife, punished with death or poverty
tmp:3230: yotze kodem zemano — emerging before one's time: premature exit from the hidden gestation (ibbur) of a new path, producing a nefel-like figure
tmp:3231: beginning to enter a path — the initial entry into a not-yet-revealed spiritual way, constituting the state of herayon (conception/pregnancy) requiring concealment
tmp:3232: herayon — pregnancy as kabbalistic symbol: the gestation-stage of a new spiritual path/teaching still concealed (linked to Prov 4:11 'be-derekh chokhmah horeitikha')
tmp:3233: studying poskim (halakhic codes) before and after innovating chiddushei Torah — the protective practice surrounding Torah novellae
tmp:3234: anshei chayil formed before and behind — the guard of 'men of valor' (cf. Song 3:7-8) generated by poskim-study, stationed around Torah novellae so no stranger (zar) approaches
tmp:3235: when a person is joyful — the state of simchah in which melancholy and sufferings are pushed aside to the periphery (setting of the dance-circle parable)
tmp:3236: the melancholy (marah shechorah) and sufferings withdrawing to the side — the displaced-but-not-transformed sorrow standing outside the circle of joy
tmp:3237: simchah ve-ha-rikkudin — the joy and dancing (the machol/dance-circle) that heals and into which even the bystander-sorrow is forcibly drawn; foretaste of the future dance
tmp:3238: cholah/machol — the dance-circle of the righteous in the World to Come, at whose head God will stand (Yerushalmi Sukkah wordplay rosh cholah)
tmp:3239: tikkun ha-cholah — rectification via the dance-circle (machol), the future perfected joy that heals illness (choleh) born of melancholy
tmp:3240: making Torah into prayer — the practice of turning learned Torah into personal supplication during hitbodedut, which generates great delight above
tmp:3241: sha'ashu'im gedolim le-ma'alah — the great supernal delight aroused Above by hitbodedut speech and turning Torah into prayer
tmp:3242: attaining great stature — the high spiritual level reached by every soul, small or great, through the practice of hitbodedut
tmp:3243: the 248 limbs (ramach evarim) — the body's limbs corresponding to the 248 positive mitzvot, each clothed with Moshe who reminds it of its mitzvah
tmp:3244: hitlabshut Moshe ba-evarim — Moshe Rabbeinu's enclothement within every limb of each Jew, prompting each limb to its mitzvah (forgotten through drunkenness)
tmp:3245: hitlabshut ha-Da'at ba-chasadim — the kabbalistic enclothement of Da'at within the chasadim (kindnesses), the structure affected by measured drinking
tmp:3246: mitpateh u-mitpayes — being appeased and conciliated: the softening/sweetening effect on judgments when Da'at is elevated through proper measured drink
tmp:3247: when the Da'at is elevated — the state of uplifted awareness/mind (via moderate drink) that raises the chasadim clothed within it
tmp:3248: the chasadim being elevated and magnified — the growth of the kindnesses that accompanies the broadening and elevation of Da'at
tmp:3249: drinking in measure according to one's capacity — moderate wine-drinking suited to one's level, which broadens Da'at rather than causing drunkenness
tmp:3250: one's mind broadened and brain elevated — the cognitive expansion (harchavat ha-da'at) produced by properly measured drinking
tmp:3251: a little drinking according to need — the small, necessary quantity of drink that benefits and broadens the mind (vs. excess)
tmp:3252: leharchiv da'ato — broadening one's Da'at/mind: expansion of consciousness as the beneficial effect of minimal drink
tmp:3254: being saved from the four traits — deliverance from idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, and evil speech (the four evils of the delayed vow, per Vayikra Rabbah on Jacob)
tmp:3255: assessing each person fairly — the just leader's practice of weighing each individual to apportion the communal burden rightly, which nullifies the four evil traits
tmp:3256: the ability to recognize a Jew among the nations — the discernment power (parallel to distinguishing which Torah may be written) to identify an ish Yisraeli among the gentiles
tmp:3257: ha-yichudim ve-ha-zivvugim — the supernal unifications and couplings (of divine partzufim), all of which are the aspect of 'nullifying the forbidden' (bittul issur)
tmp:3258: bittul issur — halakhic nullification of a forbidden admixture in the permitted, serving as symbol of supernal unification (forbidden becoming permitted, as arusah→nesuah)
tmp:3260: the loss of holy books — the burning/perishing of tzaddikim's sacred writings, likened to the Sotah scroll's divine Name erased for marital peace
tmp:3261: books erased and lost for the sake of peace between them — the sacrifice of holy writings ('My Name written in holiness') to preserve the peace of the supernal holy couple
tmp:3262: when the books are burned and lost — the tzaddikim's deliberate concealment/destruction of their Torah writings to remove the ruach kin'ah (spirit of jealousy) threatening the holy couple's union
